features.label: libwebrtc integration

patches.author: Andrew Osmond
patches.subject: Switch Android to new encoder creation strategy to only prefer platform for hardware encoders.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Gate WebRTC GMP codec creation on plugin availability.

patches.author: Michael Froman
patches.subject: Bug 2064200 (MOZ) - use AudioReceiveStreamInterface::Config.Copy() since we reuse our config

patches.author: serge-sans-paille
patches.subject: Use default operator equal implementation when possible in dom/

features.summary: Firefox now chooses Android’s platform encoder only when it provides hardware acceleration, while retaining other encoder options when appropriate. WebRTC’s GMP codec support is also enabled only when the required plugin is available, and several updates keep Firefox aligned with upstream libwebrtc configuration behavior. These are mostly compatibility and reliability improvements with little visible change for users.

features.label: WebRTC web API (RTCPeerConnection)

patches.author: Michael Froman
patches.subject: Bug 2064200 (MOZ) - upstream changed decoded_frame_counts to key_frames_decoded

patches.author: Michael Froman
patches.subject: Bug 2064200 (MOZ) - upstream changed frame_counts to decoded_frame_counts and received_frame_counts

patches.author: Michael Froman
patches.subject: Bug 2064200 (MOZ) - upstream removed implicit conversion for RtpHeaderExtensionId<->int

features.summary: Firefox updated its RTCPeerConnection WebRTC integration to match upstream libwebrtc changes in media statistics and RTP header-extension identifiers. Statistics now use clearer names such as decoded_frame_counts, key_frames_decoded, and received_frame_counts, while stricter type handling avoids relying on automatic number conversions. This keeps WebRTC connections and diagnostics working reliably as the underlying standard implementation evolves.

features.label: libwebrtc build

features.summary: Firefox’s RTCPeerConnection WebRTC implementation received a broad cleanup and reliability update: codec and RTP header-extension handling was simplified, H.264 telemetry was restored, and WebRTC statistics were moved into persistent history. RTCDataChannel objects are now kept alive correctly, and SCTP data-connection failures are surfaced as RTCError instead of being hidden. The changes also improve media negotiation and make peer-connection failures easier for applications to detect and diagnose.

features.summary: Firefox expanded WebRTC media support and codec selection, including **hardware-accelerated AV1 when the platform supports it and the preference is enabled**. MediaCapabilities checks for WebRTC and encoding now use asynchronous codec support, helping applications make more accurate choices without blocking, while Android encoder selection and GMP plugin handling were refined. The remaining changes improve code quality and correct codec metadata handling, strengthening compatibility across devices.

Changes include proper nomination handling for simplified peer setups, enforcing port restrictions to prevent data leaks, and fixing reference-counting bugs in the socket process.

features.summary: Firefox updated its SDP parser interface to use webrtc-sdp 0.3.14 and corrected how SDP image attributes are serialized so formatting state is restored afterward. This improves interoperability when WebRTC offers and answers describe media image constraints, while also removing Rust nightly warnings. _Most users will notice no visible change, but unusual negotiation cases should be handled more consistently._
